sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.1,50,00,000/- from the respondents on account of death of Mahadeva H.R., who is son of petitioners No.1 and 2, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 13-06-2022 at about 10:45 p.m., when deceased Mahadeva H.R., was returning to home after attending his work on a motorcycle bearing No. KA-02-KF-2630, on Kunigal- Maddur NH-33, from Kunigal towards Huliyurdurga, near Gavimata,
Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur, suddenly the driver of the car bearing No. KA-16-N-3914 proceeding from Huliyurdurga towards Kunigal, drove the same with high speed,
without observing any traffic rules and regulations, in rash and negligent manner,
endangering to human life and dashed to the motorcycle of deceased from opposite direction and caused accident.
Due to said impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body and was succumbed to injuries on the spot.

Earlier to the accident, the deceased was working as Deputy Sales Officer-Tumkur, at M.K. Agrotech Pvt. Ltd., (Sunpure Refined Sunflower Oil), Solur Branch and was getting salary of Rs.68,319/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.

The Kunigal Police have registered the Rajanna vs Muralidhara.P.V on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146558334/
2 case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.1,50,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 appeared through their counsel.
The respondent No.1 did not choose to file his written statement.
The respondent No.2 has filed the written statement.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing No. KA-16-N-3914 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 134(c)
and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has further contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence and the said vehicle was not having fitness certificate as on the date of accident.
It has denied the involvement of the offending vehicle.

It has contended that, the accident has occurred due to the sole negligence of the deceased who was riding the motorcycle with high speed and he was not able to control the bike and fell on the road and died on the spot and he was not wearing the helmet at the time of accident.

It has denied the age,
avocation and income of the deceased.
It is further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exaggerated.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
In view of above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Sri Mahadeva, S/o Rajanna,
succumbed to the injuries sustained in vehicular accident alleged to have occurred on 13-06-2022 at about 10.45 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-16-N-3914 ?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6.
In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 19 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19.
Further, they have got examined one more witness namely Marufuddin Sheriff as P.W.2 and closed their side.
On the other hand, the respondents No.1 and 2 have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.

3 7.
I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioners that, on 13-06-2022 at about 10:45 p.m., when deceased Mahadeva H.R., was returning to home after attending his work on a motorcycle bearing No. KA-02-KF-2630, on Kunigal-Maddur NH-33, from Kunigal towards Huliyurdurga, near Gavimata, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur, suddenly the driver of the car bearing No. KA-16-N-3914 proceeding from Huliyurdurga towards Kunigal, drove the same with high speed, without observing any traffic rules and regulations, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and dashed to the motorcycle of deceased from opposite direction and caused accident.
Due to said impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body and was succumbed to injuries on the spot.
10. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit and got marked total 19 documents as Ex.P.1 to 19.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is copy of sketch, Ex.P.5 is copy of M.V.A. report, Ex.P.6 is copy of inquest,
Ex.P.7 is copy of post- mortem report, Ex.P.8 is copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.9 are Aadhar cards (total 3), Ex.P.10 is copy of death certificate, Ex.P.11 is notarised copy of ID card, Ex.P.12 to 14 are copy of the pay slips (total 3), Ex.P.15 is copy of appointment letter with salary particulars, Ex.P.16 to 18 are copy of the attendance register for the month of April-2022, May-2022, June-2022 and Ex.P19 is copy of ID card.
11.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, except negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.
KA-16-N- 3914, the date, time and place of accident, involvement of vehicles, death of Mahadeva due to injuries caused in the accident, issuance of insurance policy and its validity are not in dispute.
Due to said impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body and was succumbed to injuries on the spot.

The Ex.P.3 spot mahazer and Ex.P.4 sketch clearly speaks that, at the time of accident the deceased Mahadeva was proceeding on his motorcycle on the left side of 36 feet width Kunigal-Maddur NH-33 road and the driver of offending car bearing No. KA-16-N-3914, coming from opposite direction, drove the same on the wrong side of the road,
Rajanna vs Muralidhara.P.V on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146558334/
4 towards his right side and dashed to the motorcycle of deceased.

The investigation officer in his final report has clearly stated that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No. Reg. KA-16-N-3914 the said accident has taken place and the deceased Mahadeva sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to said injuries on the spot.
There is absolutely no evidence placed on record by the respondents to rebut the final report of the investigation officer and other police documents produced by the petitioners.
12. The petitioner No.1, who has been examined as P.W.1, has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
The oral evidence of P.W.1 is fully corroborated with the documentary evidence marked as Ex.P.1 to 19.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

13. Further, though, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above facts in its written statement, it has not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners.

It is pertinent to note that, the P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 in his cross-examination that, the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the car bearing Reg. No.
KA-16-N-3914 and the same has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the deceased himself and he was not wearing helmet at time of accident.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not led any evidence, nor they have produced any document to show that, at the time of accident the deceased Mahadeva was not wearing helmet and there is contributory negligence on his part also.
14.
Further it is pertinent to note, as per Ex.P.5 Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the accident had not occurred due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not occurred due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of motorcycle rider, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.8, that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.
KA-16-N-3914.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence led by the respondents to disprove the case of the petitioners and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle i.e.,
deceased and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. KA-16-N-3914.

Further, the Ex.P.7 Post-motem report, clearly speaks that, deceased Mahadeva, has died due to cardio- respiratory arrest due to head injury with intracranial Haemorrhage and polytrauma sustained in the motor vehicle accident.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to deceased Mahadeva, in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

5

Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text: 16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, the deceased Mahadeva, has succumbed to the injuries sustained in motor vehicle accident occurred on 13-06-2022 at about 10:45 p.m., on Kunigal-Maddur NH-33, near Gavimata, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-16- N-3914.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.

18. Issue No.2: While answering above issue, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has already held that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that,
the alleged accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car,
bearing Reg. No. KA-16-N-3914 and due to said impact, deceased Mahadeva sustained grievous injuries on his head and was succumbed to said injuries on the spot.
Now the petitioners are required to establish that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased.
In this regard, they have produced the Aadhar card of deceased Mahadeva, and their respective Aadhar cards, which are marked as Ex.P.9.
The said documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioner No.1 is the father and petitioner No.2 is the mother of deceased Mahadeva.
The relationship of petitioners with the deceased is not in dispute.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the above documents produced by the petitioners and hold that, the petitioners are the legal heirs of deceased Mahadeva.

19. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, "The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.
Rajanna vs Muralidhara.P.V on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146558334/

6 According to Section 2(11) CPC, "legal representative" means a person who in law represents the Tractor and Trally bearing No.AP-03-AN-8690 & AP-03-AN-8712 estate of a deceased person, and includes any person who intermeddles with the estate of the deceased and where a party sues or is sued in a representative character the person on whom the estate devolves on the death of the party so suing or sued.
Almost in similar terms is the definition of legal representative under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 i.e. under Section 2(1)(g).

As observed by this Court in Custodian of Branches of BANCO National Ultramarino vs. Nalini Bai Naique [1989 Supp (2) SCC 275, the definition contained in Section 2(11) CPC is inclusive in character and its scope is wide, it is not confined to legal heirs only.

entities.text: Custodian of Branches of BANCO National Ultramarino vs. Nalini Bai Naique [1989 Supp (2) SCC 275
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Instead it stipulates that, a person who may or may not be legal heir competent to inherit the property of the deceased can represent the estate of the deceased person.
It includes heirs as well as persons who represent the estate even without title either as executors or administrators in possession of the estate of the deceased.
All such persons would be covered by the expression "legal representative".

As observed in Gujarat SRTC vs. Ramanbhai Prabhatbhai [(1987) 3 SCC 234 a legal representative is one who suffers on account of death of a person due to a motor vehicle accident and need not necessarily be a wife, husband, parent and child.

entities.text: Gujarat SRTC vs. Ramanbhai Prabhatbhai [(1987) 3 SCC 234
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Manjuri Bera (supra), in paragraph 15 of the said decision, while adverting to the provisions of Section 140 of the Act, the Court observed that even if there is no loss of dependency, the claimant, if he was a legal representative, will be entitled to compensation.
In the concurring judgment of Justice S. H. Kapadia, as His Lordship then was, it is observed that there is distinction between "right to apply for compensation" and "entitlement to compensation".
The compensation constitutes part of the estate of the deceased.
As a result, the legal representative of the deceased would inherit the estate.
Indeed, in that case, the Court was dealing with the case of a married daughter of the deceased and the efficacy of Section 140 of the Act.
Nevertheless, the principle underlying the exposition in this decision would clearly (claimants) even though they are major sons of the deceased and also earning.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

20. According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
21. The compensation towards loss of dependency: The petitioners No.1 is the father and petitioner No.2 is the mother of deceased Mahadeva.
The petitioners have established that, they are legal Rajanna vs Muralidhara.

7 representatives of the deceased.
Further, they have stated that, they were depending upon the deceased.
Hence, they are entitled to compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to calculate the loss of dependency, the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
i) Age and income of the deceased:
The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 29 years.
To substantiate this point, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.9 Aadhar Card of deceased Mahadeva, wherein the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 26-06-1992.
Admittedly, the accident took place on 13-06-2022.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the age of the deceased was about 30 years.

Further, it is averred by the petitioners that, as on the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was working as Deputy Sales Officer-Tumkur, at M.K. Agrotech Pvt. Ltd., (Sunpure Refined Sunflower Oil) Solur Branch and was getting salary of Rs.68,319/- per month.
Further it is averred that, the deceased was contributing his entire income towards maintaining his family members.

To substantiate the same the petitioners have examined the employer of the deceased i.e., Senior Manager in the department of HR and Administration as PW2 and produced notarised copy of ID card, copy of pay slips (total 3), copy of appointment letter with salary particulars, copy of attendance register for the month of April-2022,
May-2022 and June-2022, which are marked as Ex.P.11 to Ex.P.18.

On meticulously going through the said documents and evidence of P.W.2, it is very much clear that, as on the date of accident the deceased was working as Deputy Sales Officer-Tumkur, at M.K. Agrotech Pvt. Ltd., (Sunpure Refined Sunflower Oil) Solur Branch and was drawing net salary of Rs.25,703/- per month.

entities.text: Sunpure Refined Sunflower Oil) Solur Branch
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Therefore, the annual income of the deceased in the present case is held as Rs.3,08,436/-.

ii) As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the legal heirs of deceased are also entitled for future prospects of the deceased, though he was not a permanent employee as on the date of death.

National Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the deceased was aged about 30 years and was not a permanent employee, the future prospects would be 40% of his income, which comes to Rs.1,23,374/-.
Therefore, the future prospects of the deceased is held as Rs.1,23,374/-.

If this income is added to the notional income,
then it comes to Rs.4,31,810/-.
Further, the annual income of the deceased comes within the exemption limits as per Income Tax Act.
iii) The deduction of personal expenses and calculating the multiplier: The family of the deceased consist of 2 persons i.e., petitioners No.1 and 2.
The total number of the dependents of the deceased are two and admittedly the deceased has died bachelor.
Therefore, deduction towards the personal expenses of deceased is taken as 50% of the total income, which comes to Rs.2,15,905/-.
After deducting 50% out of total income, towards the personal expenses of deceased, the annual income of the deceased is held as Rs.2,15,905/-.
iv) As on the date of death, the age of the deceased was 30 years.

As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 S.C., the appropriate multiplier in the present case is taken as 17.

As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the compensation under the following conventional heads is awarded:
 a) Loss of estate - Rs. 15,000/-

b ) Loss of consortium - Rs. 40,000/-
 c) Funeral expenses - Rs. 15,000/-
The compensation under above heads has to be enhanced 10% for every 3 years.
Seven years have been lapsed from the date of the judgment.

Therefore, the compensation under the above conventional heads is enhanced by 20%, the loss of estate comes to Rs.18,000/-, the loss of filial consortium comes to Rs.48,000/- each to petitioner No.1 and 2 and funeral expenses comes to Rs.18,000/-.
22.

Accordingly, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
 Sl. Head of  Amount/Rs  No. Compensation  1. Loss of dependency Rs. 36,70,385-00  2. Loss of filial consortium Rs. 96,000-00  3. Loss of estate Rs. 18,000-00  4. Funeral expenses Rs. 18,000-00

Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs. 38,02,385/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
23. Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No. KA-16- N-3914 the accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Therefore,
the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.38,02,385/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.38,02,385/- (Rupees thirty eight lakhs two thousand three hundred and eighty five only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

The above compensation amount is apportioned as follows:
Petitioner No.1 - Father 50% Petitioner No.2 - Mother 50% Out of total compensation amount awarded in favour of petitioner No.1 and 2, 40% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in their names as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 60% amount with proportionate interest shall be released through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.1,50,00,000/- from the respondents on account of death of Mahadeva H.R., who is son of petitioners No.1 and 2, in a road traffic accident.
Due to said impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body and was succumbed to injuries on the spot.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to deceased Mahadeva, in the said accident.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
Now the petitioners are required to establish that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased.
The said documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioner No.1 is the father and petitioner No.2 is the mother of deceased Mahadeva.
The relationship of petitioners with the deceased is not in dispute.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the above documents produced by the petitioners and hold that, the petitioners are the legal heirs of deceased Mahadeva.
As observed by this Court in Custodian of Branches of BANCO National Ultramarino vs. Nalini Bai Naique [1989 Supp (2) SCC 275, the definition contained in Section 2(11) CPC is inclusive in character and its scope is wide, it is not confined to legal heirs only.
Instead it stipulates that, a person who may or may not be legal heir competent to inherit the property of the deceased can represent the estate of the deceased person.
It includes heirs as well as persons who represent the estate even without title either as executors or administrators in possession of the estate of the deceased.
All such persons would be covered by the expression "legal representative".
As observed in Gujarat SRTC vs. Ramanbhai Prabhatbhai [(1987) 3 SCC 234 a legal representative is one who suffers on account of death of a person due to a motor vehicle accident and need not necessarily be a wife, husband, parent and child.

Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs. 38,02,385/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
23. Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore,
the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.38,02,385/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
Issue No.3:

The petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.38,02,385/- (Rupees thirty eight lakhs two thousand three hundred and eighty five only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The above compensation amount is apportioned as follows:
Petitioner No.1 - Father 50% Petitioner No.2 - Mother 50% Out of total compensation amount awarded in favour of petitioner No.1 and 2, 40% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in their names as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 60% amount with proportionate interest shall be released through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
